99 Open queries

Bangla name: ওপেন কোয়ারি

← Contents

Every [UNCONFIRMED: Q-nn] marker in this documentation points to an entry here. An entry means this review could not settle the question from the code in the five repositories — not that the code is wrong. Some are gaps in the repository (an external service with no source), some are deployment or configuration values, some are genuine ambiguities in the implementation, and some are cases where the code is unambiguous but the intent is not.

Read the Kind column before acting on a query. The four kinds are:

Kind Meaning Who can answer
External The component is not in any of the five repositories BS23
Deployment The code reads a value from settings, secrets, SSM or the cloud that this review cannot see BS23 / infrastructure
Ambiguity The code is readable but its correctness or intent cannot be judged without knowing the requirement BS23 / the business
Defect The code appears wrong; this is a finding to fix, not a question to answer RVL

A Defect row is the one to prioritise. The rest are documentation debt.

2. External components — not in the repository (Q-01, Q-03, Q-05, Q-06, Q-07, Q-13, Q-34, Q-35, Q-42, Q-50)

These are the biggest structural risk in the handover: a meaningful part of the product's behaviour lives outside the five repositories, so a reader of this documentation cannot verify it.

Id Question Why it is open Cited from
Q-01 Where is the identity API source, who hosts it, and who owns it? Registration, OTP, my-profile, register-sso, allowed-app-version and delete-my-profile all go to an API that is in none of the five repositories. Locally it is http://localhost:4200/ (scripts/user-secrets.example.json). Ask BS23 for its repository, hosting and owner before go-live. X-06, X-07, X-08, X-09, X-11, P-11, U-01, U-07, primer
Q-03 Where is the Serverless / Lambda identity API source? Used by Admin login to look up user names and phones by id, and by the Booking flow. Not in any repository. X-01, X-07
Q-05 Where is the external notification service source and what does it do with the payload? The backend posts JSON to Notification:Endpoint for every SMS. The text, the channel and the templating all live there — so the platform cannot tell you what a customer actually receives. X-05, X-22, S-12
Q-06 Are the dummy external integrations still dummies in production? OneID, TSP (ticket signing) and NBR VAT are stubbed locally to https://*.invalid. Ticket signing, the OneID ticket sync and the VAT challan therefore cannot be tested end-to-end locally, and it is not visible from the code whether the real integrations are wired in a deployed environment. S-06, S-09, S-10, X-20, X-21, X-26, P-10
Q-07 Is there an agent app or client for the Agent Cognito pool? Agent accounts, the Agent-policy endpoint POST /ticketing/api/v1/offline-sold-ticket, and the OfflineSoldTickets data all exist, but no client in the five repositories uses them and nothing reads the offline-sold tickets back. Either a client is missing from the handover, or the feature is dormant. X-13, A-26
Q-13 How does the TSP client certificate (Cert/tspgw_client.pfx) reach the Ticketing pod? No project, Dockerfile or document copies it into the image. Without it the Ticketing service fails at the moment the TSP client is constructed, so this is a deployment task with a hard failure mode. S-08
Q-34 Does the user app read SocialMediaSettings, or only HeaderFooters? The user portal reads social links only from HeaderFooters; the older SocialMediaSettings record has no reader there. The app's behaviour is stated differently, and the two cannot both be right. A-30, P-01
Q-35 Which screen is the notices strip on the user portal home page actually meant to be driven by? EventApiService.getAllGeneralNotices is called and the rows are filtered in memory, but the result is assigned to a notices array that the template never binds — so the Admin screen that edits GeneralNotices (A-31) has no visible effect, while the scrolling line customers see is driven by the content editor's Notice type (A-29). Two notice features exist; the business must say which one is intended. This is the most likely reason staff would report "I published a notice and nothing happened". P-01, A-31, A-29
Q-42 Does the identity API require the static API-key header on every call, and does the portal's profile PUT really send it? GET user/my-profile sends environment.headerkey explicitly; the PUT sends no headers object at all and relies on TokenInterceptor's substring allow-list matching /user/my-profile. It works today by coincidence of the allow-list, not by design. P-11
Q-50 Which component consumes the CloudFront signed token? generate-signed-token writes one global Redis key that two admins within 60 s overwrite, and nothing in the backend reads signedToken back. Whatever validates the cookie is outside this repository. X-20

3. Deployment and configuration values (Q-02, Q-04, Q-08, Q-16, Q-19, Q-29, Q-30, Q-45, Q-49, Q-52, Q-62, Q-63, Q-69, Q-70, Q-73)

Code is unambiguous here; the value lives in secrets, SSM, the cloud account or the DNS.

Id Question Why it is open Cited from
Q-02 Is production one PostgreSQL database on schema etp, or one database per service? Every DbContext uses schema etp but each service has its own connection string. The architecture document says "one schema per service"; the code says one schema for all. This decides whether the cross-service table reads (S-17, X-24) can work at all. primer, X-24, X-26
Q-04 Does the ingress or WAF expose routes that the services leave unauthenticated? PushNotification has its authentication middleware commented out, the user-issue chat REST controller has no [Authorize], and the gateway path for the admin generate-signed-token matters. Whether these are reachable from the internet is a deployment fact. This is the single most important deployment question in the handover — see X-18. X-18, X-23, X-05, X-02, P-01
Q-08 Should the push send methods on PushNotification be live? send-to-users and send-to-user exist on the service and in the Admin client but have no caller in the five repositories. The only live sender is event publish. Dead code or a missing feature — ask which. X-23
Q-16 Does the deployed Admin base URL for the Scheduler's token cleanup include the pushnotification/ prefix? The Scheduler sends api/v1/device-token/cleanup to Services:Admin with no prefix; only PushNotification has that endpoint. If the deployed base URL does not map to PushNotification, the daily cleanup 404s and stale tokens accumulate for ever. S-13, X-23
Q-19 Is SSLCommerz in scope, and who owns its inactive callbacks? The program-settings form offers SSLCommerz and the enum supports it, but its callback handler is inactive while DgePay is the live path. Until this is answered, configure DgePay. A-03, Appendix A
Q-29 Is the raffle-draw delete a soft or a hard delete? The repository method is DeleteByIdAsync; this review did not read through to see which. It matters for whether a deleted draw can be audited. A-20
Q-30 Which time zone do the revenue reports use for day boundaries? startDate and endDate arrive as strings in GetUserBookingOrdersByEvent. Until this is known, month-end reconciliation can be off by a day. A-22
Q-45 Why do en.json and bn.json have different key counts (560 vs 587)? bn.json carries 27 keys the English file does not have, so a handful of English strings are untranslated. Confirm the intended source of truth before adding the 13th namespace. P-13
Q-49 Does the deployed gateway forward WebSocket upgrades on the portal and app chat? Both clients build SignalR with skipNegotiation: true, which means WebSockets only — no Server-Sent Events or long-polling fallback. If the ingress does not forward upgrades the chat cannot connect at all. P-12
Q-52 What format is the appLink value in, and is the store redirect intended? The force-update sheet opens appLink with url_launcher, and only when the scheme is http/https. A market:// or itms-apps:// link is silently ignored, so the customer cannot update. U-01
Q-62 Is the PushNotification service meant to be reachable without a token? All three of the app's device-token calls (POST/PUT/DELETE) go to a service whose UseAuthentication() and UseAuthorization() are commented out. On paper any caller can add or delete tokens or read another user's tokens. U-09, X-18
Q-63 Is the 2-second iOS APNs token wait long enough in production? getAPNSToken() is awaited after a fixed 2-second delay and a null token returns early, with the outer catch swallowing the failure. Whether that suffices on a real device and a real network is a deployment/environment fact this review cannot settle — locally the answer is masked by the dummy Firebase configuration. U-09, U-10
Q-69 Should the offline ticket download be paged or chunked? The download is a single request with no paging, no cursor and no signed payload, returning the whole {ticketId: checkedNumber} map. For a large stadium event this is one very large response with no progress reporting, and there is no guard on free device storage. Confirm the maximum expected event size. C-02
Q-70 What is the drift/SQLite migration story for the checker app? app_database.dart plus generated .g.dart files, with no visible migration steps. A schema change on an already-installed app therefore needs explicit handling that is not visible in the repository — confirm how shipped installs are meant to be upgraded. C-02, C-05
Q-73 Who owns VDS certificate rotation for the checker app? The trust anchor is a single PEM certificate read from .env VDS_CERTIFICATE. Rotating or adding a certificate is an app release, and any ticket signed by a previous certificate fails validation on devices that have not updated. This needs an operational owner and a rotation runbook before go-live. C-03, C-06

4. Ambiguities — readable code, unknown intent (Q-09, Q-11, Q-12, Q-15, Q-18, Q-20, Q-22–Q-28, Q-31, Q-32, Q-36–Q-41, Q-43, Q-48, Q-56, Q-57, Q-58, Q-66, Q-67)

The code says exactly what it does. What is unknown is whether that is what was meant.

Id Question Reading of the code Cited from
Q-09 What is the intended retry and dead-letter policy for the SQS consumers? RetryCount is incremented on the deserialised copy only and the message is not re-published with it, so MAX_RETRY_COUNT = 3 is never reached and a permanently failing message is retried for ever at the queue's visibility timeout. No dead-letter handling is visible in code for any consumer. S-01, S-02, S-08, S-09, S-10
Q-11 Is a paid-but-late order reconciled, or silently lost? CancelBookingAsync asks DgePay and discards the answer, cancelling every Pending/Failed order older than 12 minutes. A customer who paid after the 7–10 minute check window can end with money taken and an order cancelled. Whether anyone reconciles this by hand is not visible. S-05, P-06
Q-12 What happens to an order stuck in Requested? There is no timeout, no alert and no dead-letter for orders whose tickets never complete signing. Support finds them in the reconciliation screen. S-06, S-07, P-08
Q-15 Should a late Paid callback publish a VAT challan? The order status is only applied within 12 minutes, but the VAT message is published for any Paid callback regardless of age — so a late callback records VAT for an order that stays Pending or is later cancelled. Only DgePay-confirmed orders publish; re-check- and bypass-marked orders do not. S-10, P-06
Q-18 Should a promo code's IsActive / IsPublished flags gate its use? ValidateApplyPromoCodeAsync reads only !IsDeleted, the dates and the totals. A code staff unpublish in the admin portal still works until it is deleted or expires. S-16, P-05
Q-20 Should deleting a team in use be blocked? A team already used by an event can be soft-deleted; whether event pages still show it depends on which query reads it. A-04
Q-22 Is the bulk seat-reservation endpoint (CreateBulk, default 65 %) a real feature? No caller in the admin portal was found, and the percentage constant is unexplained. Keep it out of the interface until the business confirms. A-11
Q-23 Is the layout-before-event ordering rule enforced anywhere but the UI? A layout cannot be unpublished or deleted once its program and venue have an event, even a draft; but an event cannot be published without a published layout per active gallery. This is a UI-level rule with no database or service constraint behind it. A-13
Q-25 Does a soft-deleted promo code still block its text? ExistsAsync only checks non-deleted codes, so reusing a deleted code's text appears to be allowed. Whether that is intended is unknown. A-15
Q-26 Should deleting a checker clear their gate assignments? The delete targets Cognito only; TicketCheckerGateUsers rows survive. An orphaned assignment is invisible in the admin screen but still meaningful in the data. A-17
Q-27 Is the un-awaited Redis write loop in gate assignment a bug? Split(',').ToList().ForEach(async e => …) does not await the writes, so a fast follow-up request — or an exception — leaves TicketCheckerLevelGateMap incomplete and the checker-app sync cannot resolve the gate. A-18
Q-28 What does "duplicate" mean in the gate report? The SQL counts rows count(...) > 1 within one gate. A ticket scanned twice inside one period is one row with EntryCount 2 and is not a duplicate; a ticket scanned in two periods is. Confirm the business definition before relying on the number. A-19
Q-31 Why does the ticket-number search return an unrelated order for reserved tickets? The SQL joins on UBO."Id" = (select "BookingOrderId" from "Tickets" …), but reserved tickets store a reservation id there, so the match lands on an unrelated customer order with the same numeric id. A-23
Q-32 What is the intended session lifetime for a disabled admin? Role changes take up to the ~2 minute cache lifetime, and a disabled account's existing token stays valid until it expires because the server validates the token and does not check Cognito status per request. A-25, X-14
Q-36 Why is the event-list filter unsafe for events without segments or a venue? event.segments.filter(…) and event.venue.name are called without guards, so an event missing either breaks the browse page. P-02
Q-37 Is it intended that a refused purchase still holds the seats? CreateAsync locks the seats in Redis (12-minute lock) before validating the promo code, so a rejected code still holds inventory briefly and can show a customer a "sold out" caused by their own failed attempt. P-05
Q-38 Should the order-limit checks be exact? order_limit_exceeded fires only when the customer already has more than AllowableMaximumOrderPerUser orders, so exactly one order over the limit is allowed; seat_limit_exceeded has a comparable off-by-one. P-06
Q-39 Should machine error codes be translated for customers? err.error.title is shown verbatim, so codes like ticket_selling_stopped and order_limit_exceeded reach the customer as raw identifiers. P-06
Q-40 Should the ticket generation writes be atomic? Tickets are marked Requested and messages are published before the Booking order is set to Requested; if the Booking call fails the tickets are stranded with no parent order. P-08
Q-41 Should owner checks exist on the ticket endpoints? GetUserAllTicketStreamAsync, sync-order-to-oneid and the app equivalents take an order or ticket id with a valid token but no owner check, so any signed-in customer who learns an id can download another customer's tickets or trigger another customer's OneID sync. The impact is bounded — the PDF still goes to the order's own OneID account. P-09, P-10, U-06
Q-43 Can a customer correct a mistyped phone number or email anywhere? Both the portal and the app render name, phone and email as read-only and the PUT body has no such fields. There is no path in the product to fix a wrong phone number. P-11, U-07
Q-48 Which attachment size limit is intended, 10 MB or 5 MB? The server accepts 10 MB (ReportIssueChatManager.cs:185-186) while the portal client restricts to 5 MB (report-issue-details.component.ts:127), so a 7 MB attachment is rejected by the browser with no way to tell it was the size. No server-side MIME allowlist was found either, while the client restricts to jpeg/png/jpg/pdf — confirm whether the limit belongs on one side only. P-12, U-08
Q-56 Should the app refresh seats while the seat map is open? The app fetches a level's seats exactly once when the level is opened, with no Timer and no refresh loop, while the portal refreshes on interaction. This is the app's instance of Q-54 but is called out separately because it is the one that lets a customer act on stale availability and be refused at checkout. U-04
Q-66 Should a checker assigned to several events be able to switch between them? Multiple assignments are silently collapsed to the first (eventList.first in qr_page_view_model.dart:154 and event_page_view_model.dart:60), so a checker covering two events can only work the first with no way to switch — while the admin portal supports many-to-many assignment. Either the app or the assignment screen needs to change. C-01, A-18
Q-67 Should the leftover movie* route enum names be removed? movieList, movieDetails, movieSearch and movieBookmark in route_path.dart come from a movie-ticket template; movieList, movieDetails and movieBookmark have no feature folder behind them, and movieSearch is dead too. Confirm there is no external deep link that depends on these paths before deleting. C-01, Appendix A
Q-57 What should the app do when the gateway returns no checkoutUrl? if (paymentUrl != null) has no else, so a null checkout URL navigates nowhere and leaves the order pending with no message. U-05
Q-58 Should the app confirm payment with the server rather than infer it from the redirect? Success is decided by request.url.contains(targetUrlHostName) — substring, not prefix — and the fallback target is the production domain 'ticket-bangla.com/tickets'. A redirect that succeeds while the webhook failed is reported to the customer as a successful payment. U-05

5. Defects — code that appears wrong (Q-10, Q-14, Q-17, Q-33, Q-44, Q-46, Q-47, Q-51, Q-53, Q-54, Q-55, Q-59, Q-60, Q-61, Q-64, Q-65, Q-68, Q-71, Q-72, Q-74, Q-75, Q-76, Q-77)

These are findings, not questions. Each is reproducible from the code.

Id Finding Evidence Cited from
Q-10 Key mismatch in the payment-bypass handler. On Failed, HandleDgePaymentBypass deletes from level_locked_{EventId}_… (underscore, public event id) while everything else uses level_locked:{EventLongId}_…, so the entry is not removed and only lapses by the 12-minute rule. S-01 S-01
Q-14 Chunk index mismatch in the merge/ZIP request check. RequestMergeTicketsAsync and RequestZipTicketsAsync compute the last chunk index from the number of reservations of the level; UtilityService uses the number of tickets of this reservation. The "already generated" test therefore looks for a different file name than the worker writes. S-09 S-09
Q-17 ticketCheckerDbSync has no expiry. A pod killed mid-run leaves the flag true for ever, blocking all checker syncs until it is cleared by hand (SET ticketCheckerDbSync false). S-14 S-14
Q-33 HTML is stored unsanitised and rendered unsanitised. The Admin content editor and the notices editor store whatever HTML is sent; the portal renders Terms and Privacy with bypassSecurityTrustHtml. Anyone with the content-editor role can run script in every visitor's browser. A-29, A-31, P-03 A-29, A-31, P-03
Q-44 Database content is never translated. The language switch is client-side only — no request carries Accept-Language or a locale field — so only the portal chrome changes language. For a Bangla-first launch this is the largest single gap. P-13 P-13
Q-46 The issue-chat REST API is completely unauthenticated — in both copies. Neither UserIssue/ReportIssueChatController nor the legacy Admin/UserIssueChatController (same route api/v1/user-issue-chat, same eight endpoints) carries [Authorize], and senderId / senderName / senderType are client-supplied form fields — so an anonymous caller can post messages as ADMIN. Both SignalR hubs are authorized, so the gap is an inconsistency. This is the most serious security finding in the handover. ReportIssueChatController.cs:12, UserIssueChatController.cs:12 P-12, U-08, Appendix A
Q-47 "One issue per order" is a manager check, not a database constraint. UserIssueDbContext.cs:105 has HasIndex(p => p.PublicOrderId) without IsUnique(), and the check-then-act in the manager races. UserIssueDbContext.cs:105 P-12
Q-51 The app-version check swallows its error. The call is wrapped in try/catch and discards the exception, so a customer with no network at launch passes the force-update gate silently instead of being stopped. splash_view_model.dart:82-84 U-01
Q-53 The gallery and the home banners call the same endpoint. landing-page-image/public is invoked from two services (event_api_service_impl.dart:36, gallery_api_service_impl.dart:13), so the two screens cannot be filtered independently. U-02, U-03 U-02, U-03
Q-54 The app has no polling anywhere. The seat list, the event list and the ticket-generation status are each fetched once; the endpoints support polling but there is no Timer in the app. The portal polls; the app does not, so a customer waiting for tickets must re-open the screen. U-02, U-04, U-06 U-02, U-04, U-06
Q-55 Admin HTML is rendered unfiltered in the app. flutter_html 3.0.0 with no sanitisation configuration, in booking_details/widgets/ticket_guideline.dart:56 and event_list/widgets/warning_message.dart:87. This is the app's counterpart to Q-33. U-03 U-03
Q-59 The app passes user_id as a query parameter on GET user/my-profile, where the portal relies on the bearer token. Whether the identity API honours the query parameter or the token decides whose profile is returned. profile_api_service_impl.dart:17-22 U-07
Q-60 The two clients format dob differently — the app as yyyy-MM-dd, the portal as a full ISO timestamp — and Q-59 adds the user_id query parameter. If the identity API validates strictly, one of the two clients will fail. U-07 U-07, P-11
Q-61 delete-my-profile is implemented but unreachable. auth_api_service_impl.dart:296 calls the endpoint, but no view model or screen invokes it and no route exists. This contradicts X-11, which must be corrected — the data layer exists, the UI does not. auth_api_service_impl.dart:296 U-07
Q-64 Push handling is incomplete in the app. There is no onBackgroundMessage handler and no tap-navigation handler (getNotificationAppLaunchDetails / onMessageOpenedApp are absent), and if (message.notification == null) return; drops data-only messages. Tapping a notification opens the app but routes nowhere — so "your tickets are ready" does not take the customer to their tickets. U-10 U-10
Q-65 No read receipt exists. The app makes no API call when a notification arrives, and there is no read-receipt endpoint in the platform. The platform cannot tell whether a customer saw the ticket-ready notification, which matters for the S-12 support workflow. U-10 U-10
Q-68 The -1 manual-entry convention is undocumented. state.isManual ? -1 : 1 is the only place manual entries are distinguished on the wire, and nothing in the backend documents or validates the sign. Confirm with BS23 what -1 means to the server before changing it — gate reports depend on it. qr_repository_impl.dart:24-26 C-02, C-04, C-05
Q-71 A missing QR label throws instead of showing "incorrect QR". .where((e) => e.label == "…").toList().single raises on zero or multiple matches, so a malformed or third-party QR produces an unhandled exception rather than a friendly message. qr_page_view_model.dart C-03
Q-72 iOS cannot verify any QR code. AppDelegate.swift (13 lines) registers plugins only — there is no certificate/methods handler and no Swift implementation. Every verifyQrData throws, is caught, returns null, and every ticket is reported incorrect. The checker app is Android-only for real validation until a Swift verifyCertificate is written. This is not a barcode-scanner limitation. AppDelegate.swift:1-13 C-03, C-06
Q-74 Duplicate scanning is detected only locally, by count > 0. Two devices at the same gate with the same download can both accept the same ticket; the server is only told later by the sync. C-03 C-03
Q-75 A manual entry skips VDS signature verification entirely. The signature path exists only in onQRCodeDetected; manual entry goes straight to the local-map lookup. A checker can therefore accept any ticket id present in the downloaded set, printed or not — and an unknown id is still written to the database, becoming a later -1 report for a ticket that does not exist. The commented-out length validation widens this further. C-04 C-04
Q-76 A failed sync still updates "last sync time". _lastSyncTime is set unconditionally before the result is known, so the UI can claim a successful sync that never happened. The scans themselves are safe — only the displayed time lies. There is also no retry backoff and no failure counter. qr_page_view_model.dart:129 C-05
Q-77 Is /manualTicketValidation intended for admissions? It proves authenticity only — not event, not gate, not already-used. Anyone using it to admit customers would admit a used or wrong-gate ticket. It should be labelled as a diagnostic tool in the UI. C-06 C-06
